description: The Karnataka State Remote Sensing Applications Centre has called bids for a pilot using satellite imagery, drones and AI to map crops, detect pests and diseases and estimate village-level yields
body_lead: Karnataka plans to introduce satellite-based crop monitoring and yield estimation, especially in drought-hit regions, to improve agricultural planning and crop-loss assessment. The Karnataka State Remote Sensing Applications Centre (KSRSAC) has recently invited bids from firms, agencies and startups to develop and demonstrate the system. To be launched under the CM Raitha Chaitanya Karnataka Agritech Mission 2026, the pilot will cover two crop seasons — Rabi 2026-27 and Kharif 2027-28 — across two study areas of around 500 sq km each.
